claims.claim: RecurrentGemma uses the Griffin architecture, which combines linear recurrences with local attention and has a fixed-size state
claims.quote: Griffin combines linear recurrences with local attention to achieve excellent performance on language. It has a fixed-sized state, which reduces memory use and enables efficient inference on long sequences.
claims.ablation_quote: Gemma-2B was trained on 3T tokens and Gemma-7B was trained on 6T tokens, while both RecurrentGemma-2B and RecurrentGemma-9B were trained on 2T tokens.

claims.claim: Release of 2B and 9B models, each with pre-trained and instruction-tuned variants
claims.quote: We provide two sizes of models, containing 2B and 9B parameters, and provide pre-trained and instruction tuned variants for both.

claims.claim: Performance comparable to Gemma despite being trained on fewer tokens
claims.quote: Our models achieve comparable performance to similarly-sized Gemma baselines despite being trained on fewer tokens.

claims.claim: Faster inference than Gemma models because the state is compressed to a fixed size
claims.quote: RecurrentGemma compresses input sequences into a fixed-size state without sacrificing performance. This reduces memory use and enables efficient inference on long sequences.

claims.claim: Release of efficient JAX code, including a specialized Pallas kernel for the linear recurrence on TPUs, plus a PyTorch reference implementation
claims.quote: including a specialized Pallas kernel to perform the linear recurrence on TPUs. We provide a reference PyTorch implementation as well.

data_disclosure.quote: We use the same pre-training data as the Gemma models, which comprises primarily English data from web documents, mathematics and code.

tokens_disclosed.quote: We provide two sizes of RecurrentGemma, with 2B and 9B parameters, both trained on 2T tokens.

coding.note: Ablation for the Griffin architecture is coded PARTIAL, not YES. The only comparison is against Gemma, and it is confounded: the token counts differ (2T vs 3T/6T) and the architecture differs in more than one way. Two items were left out of the claims because they appear outside the abstract and introduction: the 'novel RLHF algorithm' (Instruction tuning section) and the sqrt(width) embedding scaling (Model architecture section). The paper does not say whether the Gemma scores were re-run or copied, so rerun and scores_copied are NR. The human evaluation and the 'independent team' safety review were both run internally, so third_party is NO. Compute is N because hardware is reported only for inference benchmarks, not for training.
